A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TextMesh4D and contain matching methods, experiments, and principal displays despite the changed title. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable throughout. The supplied v2 ends with references; v3 additionally contains Appendices A–C.

before.justification: v2 reports original mesh-generation experiments, CLIP and GPT-4V evaluations, a 31-participant user study, and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds CT4D preference scores and additional generated examples in its appendix.

M1.justification: The stated global LGSR objective changes in Equation 4: v2 penalizes deviation from identity, whereas v3 penalizes deviation from the optimized canonical Jacobians using an explicit Frobenius norm. The two-stage JDF/Poisson pipeline and local ARAP term remain. The PDFs do not establish whether this written objective revision reflects an implementation change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate text-to-4D generation using the union of baseline prompt sets. v3 enumerates 48 study prompts and displays additional examples within the existing object and motion coverage; it does not establish an expansion of the underlying task or dataset.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same nine baselines, including 3-to-4D. v3 Appendix B adds an actual quantitative CT4D comparison in Table 3 and a visual comparison in Figure 9. v2 excludes CT4D quantitatively and only refers to a supplementary qualitative comparison absent from the supplied PDF.

E3.justification: Appendix B introduces GPT-4V preference evaluation against CT4D using published images. Appendix A1 also qualifies v2's official-code/default-configuration statement by reporting a 3-to-4D reimplementation. Neither establishes a rerun of retained experiments. The newly specified 48 prompts and 1–5 rating scale document the existing user study.

E4.justification: Figure 7 and Table 2 retain the same vertex-parameterization and local/global-regularizer ablations, with identical results. The new topology-change boundary discussion supplies no separately documented robustness experiment or tested failure case; the appendix comparisons are additional benchmark evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix A2 newly reports participant age as 26.3 ± 1.5 years, without defining the ± statistic. This is a limited addition to descriptive statistical reporting. Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the generation and preference results.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1 and 2 are unchanged. New Table 3 reports GPT-4V preferences over CT4D of 64.1%, 79.2%, 68.4%, 88.2%, and 80.7% for AQ, SQ, MQ, TA, and Overall. Figures 8–9 add qualitative results; these are additional comparisons, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 4 revises the mathematical reference for global regularization. Appendix C also supplies explicit definitions of the previously named temporal-smoothness and degrees-of-freedom penalties. The Poisson least-squares formulation remains unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list qualify the novelty claim as the first zero-shot text-to-4D mesh framework and recast JDF from freeing deformation from topology to topology-aware recovery enforcing integrability. The central JDF/LGSR contributions, claimed quality advantages, and single-24GB-GPU claim remain.

C2.justification: v3 substantially revises the explanation of topology's role: Poisson integration uses connectivity to suppress inconsistent diffusion guidance. Section 5 also replaces v2's mainly stability-versus-diversity explanation for extreme-motion failures with an explicit representational boundary: fixed connectivity cannot faithfully express splitting, merging, breaking, or new parts. This materially clarifies the mechanism and applicability limits.

D1.justification: Appendices A and C supply previously absent study instructions, the 48-prompt list, rating scale, baseline implementation exceptions, LoRA-based VSD details, and loss formulas. Section 4.1 changes RTX 6000 to RTX A5000, matching the already-existing Table 1 entry. v2's future code-release promise disappears; neither PDF provides access to the proposed method's code.

R1.justification: v3 adds Kerbl et al.'s 3D Gaussian Splatting reference and removes several introductory diffusion citations, including Stable Video Diffusion, Imagen Video, and DDIM. The principal related-work survey remains, with more explicit zero-shot positioning. Publication and citation-style updates largely concern already-cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around 4D data scarcity, physical understanding, and inconsistent diffusion guidance. v3 introduces a separate Discussion section and organized appendices, revises method explanations, and changes the title, author/affiliation block, and citation style. This is substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: The overview diagram is substantially redrawn, and v2 Figure 3 becomes the front-page teaser in v3. The conference layout adds running headers and relocates retained figures and tables. Figures 8–9 and Table 3 are added, while Table 1's caption is corrected to describe its broader comparator set.

improvement.justification: v3 improves assessability through clearer canonical-Jacobian mathematics, explicit loss and user-study documentation, and a useful fixed-topology applicability boundary. These address ambiguities in v2. The CT4D addition provides limited validation because it uses published images with sparse evaluation details, while Section 4.2 still broadly states that CT4D is excluded quantitatively. The net gain is a better documented and more carefully qualified paper.
